html:
The Carthaginian Empire was the sea power built by Carthage, a Phoenician city in what is now Tunisia. On the map from 500 to 300 BCE it holds the coast of North Africa, southern Spain, western Sicily, Sardinia and the Balearic Islands.

Settlers from Tyre in the Phoenician cities founded Carthage, by tradition in 814 BCE. As Phoenicia fell under Assyria and Babylon, Carthage became the leader of the western Phoenician colonies, such as Gadir in Spain. By the 500s BCE it ran a network of ports and trading posts, guarded by a strong navy, and grew rich on metals, farming and trade.

It fought the Greek cities of Sicily on and off for two centuries, and then Rome. The First Punic War cost it Sicily. In the Second, Hannibal crossed the Alps and beat the Romans in Italy, but lost in the end. In 146 BCE Rome destroyed Carthage and took its land as the province of Africa.
